messages:
Anya: Quick follow-up from the API-key vs RBAC RFC — thinking about a pragmatic migration path for service auth. TL;DR: we need a short-lived shim so product teams don't break and a clear long-term plan to map keys to role bindings.
Tom: +1. can you sketch the shim? do we punt to a proxy or extend the auth service?
Anya: Proposal: service-auth-proxy that accepts existing API keys and emits ephemeral actor claims to the backend. It would do introspect -> emit JWT with `svc` claim. Long-term target is eliminating key surface by moving to role bindings in the identity system.
Priya: Sounds good. main concern is audit/traceability and perf. Proxy adds latency and a single extra hop.
Anya: Agreed. Perf numbers matter. We keep the proxy in-path only for legacy keys; new traffic uses direct mTLS/JWT. We can add caching of introspection results and short-lived tokens to reduce calls.
Jorge: For mapping — how do we represent key intent? Right now keys are just a blob tied to project/org. We need a deterministic translation to roles. Example: key -> (project:foo, purpose:ingest) -> bind `role:svc.ingest` at project:foo.
Lina: We should avoid creating a role per key. Roles are templates (svc.ingest) and bindings are per-principal (service). Migration: create a service principal per key, attach role bindings, then prefer principal-based auth.
Tom: Migration steps I'd expect: 1) shadow proxy that logs mapping decisions, 2) create service principals for keys, 3) attach roles by heuristics (owner input), 4) opt-in cutover, 5) eventual unilateral deprecation of keys.
Priya: On heuristics: maybe use existing metadata (key name, created_by, last_used) + ask owners during migration window. Also surface in Console a list of suggested bindings.
Anya: Example introspect -> emit flow (pseudo):
```
POST /introspect
body: {api_key: "..."}
returns: {principal_id: "svc-123", scope: ["project:foo"], metadata: {purpose: "ingest"}}
// proxy issues ephemeral JWT: {sub: "svc-123", roles: ["svc.ingest"], exp: now + 30s}
```
Jorge: Do we need to handle cross-project tokens? Some keys are org-wide. How do we scope roles?
Lina: Keep role bindings namespaced: `org:billing -> role:svc.invoicer`, `project:foo -> role:svc.ingest`. The proxy must include the allowed scope in the emitted claim, don't expand beyond that.
Tom: Questions on RBAC primitives: do we add a `service` actor type + `binding` objects? I think yes — we already have user/org bindings; extend for services with `actor_type=service`.
Priya: Auditing: every proxy issuance should write an audit event with request id, key id (hashed), emitted principal, and mapping rationale (heuristic or manual). We need retention policy and alerting for suspicious mappings.
Anya: Ops concerns: how do we run the proxy? Hosted: run in our infra with HA and autoscale; Dedicated/private: offer it as an appliance component or lightweight binary that teams can run next to their control plane.
Jorge: Backward compatibility: we need a header `X-Legacy-Key-Used: true` until deprecate. Also have a debug mode to print mapping decisions for owners.
Lina: Security detail: rotate underlying keys, and make sure proxy can revoke mapping instantly. Add a revocation cache and realtime invalidation hook.
Tom: Migration UI: Console should show candidate principal + suggested roles + owners + one-click approve. Without this I don't want to auto-bind anything.
Priya: Will add telemetry requirements: latency p95 target for proxy < 20ms overhead, cache hit ratio goal 95% for common workloads, and metric `mapping_suspect_count` for anomalies.
Anya: Next actions: I'll draft an RFC for the shim + migration UI. Priya/Tom/Jorge — can you review the perf/audit bits? Lina — can you sketch the service-principal data model? I'll include a prototype sequence diagram.
security-bot: New RFC draft posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/serv-auth-shim-2026 (comment thread open) :eyes:
Tom: Great — I'll review today.
Jorge: I'll start a small spike to enumerate keys and heuristics for a single product team.
Lina: I'll sketch the model by EOD and drop a short JSON schema in thread.
Anya: Thanks all. We'll sync Friday for decision on the initial rollout window. :calendar:
